title: Async-to-sync cancellation needs an explicit outcome before notification
applies_when: A Python coroutine bridge stores a result or exception in a slot and signals an event in finally, while a blocking caller interprets an untouched slot as a successful None result.
lesson: Trace the outcome channel as well as the wakeup. Since Python 3.8, asyncio.CancelledError derives from BaseException, so except Exception does not publish it. A finally notification can wake the blocking caller while its result slot still contains the initial None. Reproduce through the complete imported bridge and a real generated synchronous backend method, not a copied catch block. Preserve normal values, original ordinary exceptions, cancellation cleanup and a subsequent healthy call. If the bridge already has an exception-delivery contract, explicitly store CancelledError so that existing caller-side propagation can raise it; do not equate a set event with successful completion.
avoid_when: Do not catch all BaseException merely to cover asyncio cancellation: KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit can have different control-flow contracts. A backend cancelling itself and a synchronous caller interrupting a running backend are opposite directions; similar cancellation wording does not establish duplicate ownership. Transporting a cancellation outcome does not add cancellation requests, wait for every child task, force-stop blocking I/O or prove bulk-operation cleanup. The linked fix is proposed, not merged; focused Windows/Linux native controls and a Windows project selection do not establish full CI, every remote protocol or better Scout recall/cost. This is an owner-led finding, not a prospective selector result.

evidence.note: Documents cancellation semantics and the BaseException inheritance change in Python 3.8. Catching ordinary Exception alone therefore cannot populate a cancellation outcome.
Pinned _runner publishes only Exception then always signals its event; sync starts with a None slot and already propagates stored BaseException objects. This identifies the complete bridge mechanism.

One-line explicit cancellation handling plus regressions for direct cancellation, real Task.cancel/finally, backend info and recovery. Reports a focused six-case Linux original/fixed comparison and 190-pass Windows selection; full CI and remote-storage integration are not claimed.

Distinct proposal cancels the submitted future when the synchronous event wait raises KeyboardInterrupt. It does not implement worker-to-caller cancellation outcome delivery; neither proposal establishes safety of every combined platform path.
